newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close lower following cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close lower following cash.

text.p: CME lumber futures were pressured by the weak cash market Friday and set new daily lows late before closing weak, traders said.
Futures closed $6.80 to $1.60 per tbf lower with May off most at $394.70 and July off $3.50 at $395.00 per tbf.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $399 per tbf, off $7 from midweek and $11 under last Friday's level.

The weak cash trend was expected to continue. Traders cited reports of wholesalers selling wood under $390, and mills that had been holding firm also eased asking prices. Mills found no takers at the higher price levels, cash sources added.

The National Association of Realtors reported early Friday that March U.S. existing home sales fell 2.8 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.11 million units. The group attributed the drop in last month's home sales activity to adverse weather conditions in some parts of the country and to an increase in interest rates.
